categories.label: Filing Formalities
categories.prompt: Assess Form 28 for this SLP (Civil): court and jurisdiction caption, party positions, the petition body, mandatory declarations, grounds, prayers, and any supporting affidavit this task names. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score other Form 28 points, other categories, or legal merit.

categories.label: Advocate's Check List
categories.prompt: Assess the Advocate's Check List and the Advocate-on-Record's certificate on this filing, including the signature block. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Listing Proforma
categories.prompt: Assess the Listing Proforma (Proforma for First Listing) that accompanies the filing. Decide only whether the columns or particulars named in this task are duly filled. Do not score other listing fields unless this task names them.

categories.label: Petition Presentation
categories.prompt: Assess the form of the petition: paper, spacing, font, margins, numbering, signatures and endorsements. Decide only the objection in the user message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Applications
categories.prompt: Assess interlocutory or miscellaneous applications named in this task (condonation, substitution, caveat, permission to appear). Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Annexures
categories.prompt: Assess the annexures: markings, true copies, order, and match to the Index or List of Dates. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Parties and Cause Title
categories.prompt: Assess the cause title, Memo of Parties, and party particulars named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Drafting and Execution Dates
categories.prompt: Assess the drafting date of the petition relative to filing, the supporting affidavit and the Vakalatnama. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Index and Paper Book
categories.prompt: Assess the common index, running pagination, and Part I / Part II (or volume) arrangement of the paper book. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Limitation
categories.prompt: Assess the Office Report on Limitation and any condonation of delay for a time-barred petition named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Affidavit
categories.prompt: Assess the supporting affidavit named in this task: presence, form, swearing, exhibits and blanks. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Translations
categories.prompt: Assess translations of vernacular documents, official translation or exemption, and translated powers of attorney. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Vakalatnama
categories.prompt: Assess the Vakalatnama: execution, acceptance, executant particulars and related endorsements. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Memo of Appearance
categories.prompt: Assess the Memo of Appearance named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: List of Dates
categories.prompt: Assess the List of Dates and Events named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

defects.defect: The Appeal is not accompanied by the Certified copy of the impugned order passed by the Armed Forces Tribunal
defects.requirement: A statutory appeal under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act must include a certified copy of the impugned judgment or order under Supreme Court Circular F.No.4/Judl./2026 read with Order XIX Rules 3(2) and 40 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. Section 31 of the Armed Forces Tribunal Act separately governs leave to appeal; Section 30 does not itself prescribe the certified-copy requirement.
defects.trigger_words: ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL; Certified to be true copy; Certified Copy; O.A. No.; Original Application No.; PRINCIPAL BENCH; REGIONAL BENCH
where_to_look: Impugned Order: certification of the Armed Forces Tribunal's order
The endorsement on the order such as "Certified to be true copy" or "Certified Copy", with the copying section's stamp, seal and date of issue.
A valid copy is the Tribunal's own order, headed "ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL" with its O.A. number, bearing that certification.
The order under appeal, matched to the Tribunal, case number and date stated in the Synopsis and List of Dates, not an order of another forum.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to upload the certified copy of the impugned order passed by the Armed Forces Tribunal.

If the copy filed is a plain, downloaded or uncertified copy: Option for the User to upload and replace the impugned order with a corrected version, namely the certified copy issued by the Armed Forces Tribunal.

Option for the User to mark this defect as complete if the filing is not an appeal against an order of the Armed Forces Tribunal, or the certified copy is already filed at another page of the case file.
defects.applicable_rule: Order XIX Rules 3(2) and 40, Supreme Court Rules, 2013; Section 31, Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007
defects.location_source: Supreme Court Circular F.No.4/Judl./2026 dated 20 March 2026; Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order XIX Rules 3(2) and 40; Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007, Sections 30-31
defects.ai_note:
The Armed Forces Tribunal's order usually opens with the heading "ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL", the bench name and the O.A. number; a certified copy carries an endorsement such as "Certified to be true copy" or "Certified Copy" with the copying section's stamp, seal and date of issue. Labels may be wrong; identify the Impugned Order by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the order of the Armed Forces Tribunal that is under appeal and (b) that copy being a certified copy issued by the Tribunal.
Do not treat a plain or downloaded copy, or an order of another forum, as the certified copy, or rely on a Synopsis or List of Dates line that only mentions the order. Stamps and seals are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections for the certification stamp or seal.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when the shown pages of the order positively show that it is uncertified, such as a copy marked as downloaded, or its first and last pages are shown and neither bears a certification or seal; quote that line. Return compliant when the shown excerpts show the order with a certification or seal; quote it. Return needs_review when the order or its certification is not in the excerpts or is illegible.

defects.main_category: SLP (Civil), SLP (Criminal), Civil Appeal, Criminal Appeal, Writ Petition (Civil),Writ Petition (Criminal), Transfer Petition (Civil), Transfer Petition (Criminal), Review Petition (Civil), Review Petition (Criminal), Original Suit (Civil),  Contempt Petition (Civil), Contempt Petition (Criminal), Election Petition (Civil), Arbitration Petition, Curative Petition (Civil), Curative Petition (Criminal)
defects.defect: The present petition is being filed after the expiry of the prescribed period of thirty days from the date of the dismissal order.
defects.requirement: Under Order XVI Rule 4(1) of the Rules, a petition praying that an appeal dismissed for default of appearance be restored may be presented only within thirty days of the order of dismissal.
defects.trigger_words: dismissed for default; default of appearance; dismissed for non-prosecution; restoration of the appeal; Order XVI Rule 4; Date of filing; recall the order
where_to_look: Main Petition: date of the dismissal order and the date of filing
Record of Proceedings: order dismissing the appeal for default
The date at the head of the dismissal order in the Record of Proceedings, the date below the prayer of the restoration petition, and any delay stated in the Office Report on Limitation.
A valid filing falls within thirty days of the dismissal order; count the days from the order's date to the date of filing.
The restoration petition and the dismissal order that bear this appeal's Supreme Court case number, not orders passed in other matters.
Supreme Court Registry filing/refiling history or the relevant Registry order: use authoritative presentation dates and any period actually allowed; do not use a drafting date as proof of filing.
Return needs_review when the governing period or an authoritative date required for the calculation is unavailable.
how_to_cure: Prompt the User to confirm whether the petition for restoration is being filed beyond thirty days from the date of the dismissal order. If yes:         1. option for Jubeex to auto-draft an application for condonation of delay in filing the restoration petition.
2. Option for the User to upload the application for condonation of delay in filing the restoration petition.
defects.location_source: Page 82 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Order XVI Rule 4 (1) - An appellant whose appeal has been dismissed for default of appearance may, within thirty days of the order, present a petition praying that the appeal may be restored and the Court may, after giving notice of
such application to the respondent who has entered appearance in the appeal, restore the appeal if good and
sufficient cause is shown, putting the appellant on terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks fit, or pass such other order as the circumstances of the case and the ends of justice may require.
defects.ai_note:
The restoration petition usually seeks "restoration of the appeal" or to "recall the order" and cites Order XVI Rule 4; the dismissal order in the Record of Proceedings reads "dismissed for default" or "dismissed for non-prosecution" under its date. The Office Report on Limitation may state the date of filing and any delay. Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the date of the order dismissing the appeal for default of appearance, (b) the date the restoration petition was presented and (c) the second falling within thirty days of the first.
Do not take the date of another hearing, a dismissal on merits, or the date a copy was received as the dismissal date; count from the order itself.
Return not_applicable when the shown petition is not one to restore an appeal dismissed for default of appearance. Return defect_found only when both dates are legible and the petition was presented more than thirty days after the dismissal order, or the Office Report on Limitation shows that delay; quote the dismissal order's date line and the filing date. Return compliant when both dates are legible and the gap is thirty days or less. Return needs_review when either date is not in the excerpts or is illegible.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 fails to set out the facts and particulars of the case chronologically and in separate paragraphs.
defects.requirement: A request under Section 11(4), 11(5), or 11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as applicable, must state concisely and in separate paragraphs the facts and particulars of the case in chronological order, in accordance with the Appointment of Arbitrators by the Chief Justice of India Scheme, 1996.
defects.trigger_words: MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH; FACTS OF THE CASE; BRIEF FACTS; STATEMENT OF FACTS; arbitration clause; GROUNDS
where_to_look: Main Petition: facts set out in separate numbered paragraphs
The numbered paragraphs under "MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH" or a "FACTS" heading, up to the grounds and the prayer.
A valid statement gives each fact its own concise paragraph, with the dated events running in order from earliest to latest.
The Section 11 petition bearing this matter's Supreme Court cause title, not facts reproduced from earlier correspondence between the sides.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-edit the petition to split facts in chronological order and into numbered paragraphs
2. Option for User to edit the Petition with Jubeex.
defects.applicable_rule: Appointment of Arbitrators by the Chief Justice of India Scheme, 1996, paragraphs 2-3
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: We will mark it when paragraph numbers are not given
defects.ai_note:
The facts usually follow "MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH" or a heading such as "FACTS OF THE CASE", "BRIEF FACTS" or "STATEMENT OF FACTS", each paragraph carrying a number and often opening "That". Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the facts and particulars of the case set out in separate paragraphs, (b) stated concisely and (c) arranged in chronological order.
Do not judge the order of events from the grounds or the prayer, which may argue points out of date order; only the facts portion counts. A single long paragraph that narrates several dated events in one block is not a statement in separate paragraphs.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when the shown facts paragraphs positively show unnumbered or merged paragraphs, or a dated event placed after a later one; quote the paragraph where the order breaks. Return compliant when the shown facts paragraphs are separate, concise and in date order throughout. Return needs_review when the facts portion is not in the excerpts, is illegible, or only a fragment is shown so that the order cannot be judged.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 is not accompanied by the original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy thereof;
defects.requirement: A Petition under Section 11 must be accompanied, in its Annexures, by the original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy of it.
defects.trigger_words: ARBITRATION AGREEMENT; arbitration clause; DISPUTE RESOLUTION; shall be referred to arbitration; IN WITNESS WHEREOF; TRUE COPY; Certified copy
where_to_look: Annexures: original or duly certified copy of the arbitration agreement
Main Petition: date and description of the arbitration agreement
The arbitration clause in the agreement, often headed "ARBITRATION" or "DISPUTE RESOLUTION", and the facts paragraph of the petition that gives the agreement's date.
A valid entry is the original agreement or a copy bearing a certification, whose date matches the agreement described in the petition.
The Annexure that reproduces the agreement itself, not a petition paragraph that only quotes or summarises the arbitration clause.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to upload the Original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy of the same.
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.ai_note:
The arbitration agreement may be a stand-alone "ARBITRATION AGREEMENT" or a contract with an arbitration clause, often headed "ARBITRATION" or "DISPUTE RESOLUTION" and reading "shall be referred to arbitration"; a certified copy carries an endorsement such as "Certified copy". If it is not clearly titled, match it by the date the petition gives. Labels may be wrong; identify the Annexure by its own heading and the cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the arbitration agreement, or the agreement containing the arbitration clause, filed with the petition and (b) that document being the original or a duly certified copy.
Do not accept a petition paragraph that only quotes the arbitration clause, or another contract or letter whose date does not match the agreement described in the petition. Signatures and seals are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when the shown Annexure reproducing the agreement positively shows that it is neither the original nor a certified copy, such as an unsigned draft or a bare extract; quote that line. Return compliant when the shown excerpts show the agreement with its arbitration clause, as the signed original or with a certification. Return needs_review when the agreement is not in the excerpts, is illegible, or is shown without its signature or certification page.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 does not state the names and addresses of the parties
defects.requirement: A Petition under Section 11 must be accompanied by the names and addresses of the parties to the arbitration agreement.
defects.trigger_words: IN THE MATTER OF; Versus; R/o; Registered Office at; Through its; MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH
where_to_look: Main Petition: names and addresses of parties to the arbitration agreement
Memo of Parties: name and full address of each party
The cause title from "IN THE MATTER OF" down to "MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH" or "The Humble Appeal of the Appellant Named Above", and the facts paragraphs that introduce the parties.
A valid entry gives every party to the arbitration agreement a name and a full address; compare the cause title with the parties the facts describe as bound by the agreement.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-fill the names & addresses of all parties (it shall pick up the same from the annexed arbitration agreement)
2. Option for the user to edit the petition to insert the particulars
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: Address of the parties should be uniform across the entire case file
defects.ai_note:
Names and addresses usually sit in the cause title below "IN THE MATTER OF", or in the Memo of Parties, on either side of "Versus" with "R/o", "Registered Office at" or "Through its", ending at "MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH" or "The Humble Appeal of the Appellant Named Above". In a table a blank cell is not printed: a party row with a name but no address field shows the address was left blank. Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the name of each party to the arbitration agreement and (b) the address of each such party.
Do not count an advocate's address as the party's own address, or treat a person named in the facts who is not a party to the arbitration agreement as a required party.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when a shown entry gives a party with no address, or the facts name a party to the agreement missing from the list; quote that entry. Return compliant when the shown excerpts give a name and address for every party to the agreement. Return needs_review when the cause title or Memo of Parties is not in the excerpts, is illegible, or only part of the party list is shown.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 is not accompanied by the names and addresses of the Arbitrators, if any, already appointed
defects.requirement: Where any arbitrator has already been appointed, a Petition under Section 11 must be accompanied by the names and addresses of the arbitrators so appointed.
defects.trigger_words: appointed as the sole arbitrator; nominee arbitrator; nominated; Arbitral Tribunal; letter of appointment; presiding arbitrator
where_to_look: Main Petition: names and addresses of arbitrators already appointed
Annexures: letter or order appointing an arbitrator, with its date
The facts paragraphs describing the invocation of arbitration and any appointment or nomination of an arbitrator.
A valid entry names each appointed arbitrator with an address; where the facts refer to an appointment letter or order, its date should match an Annexure.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-fill names & addresses of Arbitrators already appointed into the facts paragraph of the main petition (the same can be picked up from an appointment letter)
2. Option for the user to edit the petition to insert the particulars
3. Option to mark as not applicable if no arbitrators appointed
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: VW: Note to Tech-Will it possible for the tool to read the Petition and ascertain if any Arbitrator has been already appointed?
defects.notes_2: Note from tech - We can do this it is possible but will need to specify to  the Agent to read the petition, so basically create a workflow for it
defects.ai_note:
An existing appointment usually appears in the facts as "appointed as the sole arbitrator", "nominated as its arbitrator" or "nominee arbitrator", or in an Annexure such as a letter of appointment or an order constituting the Arbitral Tribunal, identified by the date the facts give for it. Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs, where any arbitrator has already been appointed, (a) the name of each such arbitrator and (b) the address of each such arbitrator.
Do not treat a proposed name, a panel of names offered for selection, or a request to appoint as an appointment already made, and do not take an advocate's address for the arbitrator's address.
Return not_applicable when the shown excerpts positively show that no arbitrator has yet been appointed. Return defect_found only when the excerpts show an arbitrator already appointed and the shown petition paragraph describing that appointment gives no name or no address for that arbitrator; quote that line. Return compliant when the name and address of every appointed arbitrator are shown. Return needs_review when the appointment facts are not in the excerpts, are illegible, or only some of the appointed arbitrators are shown.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 is not accompanied by the name and address of the person or institution to whom any function has been entrusted by the parties under the appointment procedure agreed upon by them.
defects.requirement: Where the arbitration agreement entrusts any function under the agreed appointment procedure to a person or institution, a Petition under Section 11 shall be accompanied by the name and address of that person or institution.
defects.trigger_words: appointing authority; appointment procedure; arbitration clause; nominated by; Arbitration Centre; under the Rules of
where_to_look: Main Petition: name and address of the person or institution entrusted
Annexures: arbitration agreement clause on the appointment procedure
The arbitration clause naming an appointing authority, institution or person, and the facts paragraphs of the petition that describe that clause.
A valid entry gives the entrusted person's or institution's name and address in the petition, matching the authority named in the agreement's clause.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-fill names & addresses of persons/institution in the facts of the main petition
2. Option for the user to edit the petition to insert the particulars
3.  Option to mark as not applicable if no person/instituiton entrusted
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: VW: Note to Tech-Will it be possible for the tool to read the Petition and ascertain the Institution.
defects.notes_2: Note from tech - We can do this it is possible but will need to specify to  the Agent to read the petition, so basically create a workflow for it
defects.ai_note:
The entrusted person or institution usually appears in the arbitration clause as an "appointing authority", an arbitration centre or council, or a named officer who is to nominate the arbitrator, often with words such as "nominated by" or "under the Rules of"; the petition's facts often restate that clause. Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition and the agreement by their own headings and the cause title.
Compliance needs, where any function under the agreed appointment procedure is entrusted to a person or institution, (a) the name of that person or institution and (b) its address, stated with the petition.
Do not treat an arbitrator already appointed, the advocate for either side, or a court named only as the forum for disputes as the person or institution entrusted under the appointment procedure.
Return not_applicable when the shown arbitration clause positively shows that no function is entrusted to any person or institution. Return defect_found only when the shown clause entrusts a function to a person or institution and the shown petition paragraph describing it omits that name or address; quote both lines. Return compliant when the shown excerpts give the name and address of the entrusted person or institution. Return needs_review when the clause or the petition's description of it is not in the excerpts or is illegible.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 does not state the qualifications required of the arbitrators by the agreement of the parties
defects.requirement: Where the arbitration agreement requires the arbitrators to hold any qualification, a Petition under Section 11 must be accompanied by a statement of the qualifications so required.
defects.trigger_words: qualification; shall be a retired; retired Judge; having experience in; arbitration clause; shall be a person
where_to_look: Main Petition: qualifications the agreement requires of the arbitrators
Annexures: arbitration agreement clause on arbitrator qualifications
The arbitration clause of the arbitration agreement, or of an agreement between the sides that contains one, and the facts paragraphs of the petition describing that clause.
A valid entry restates in the petition every qualification the clause prescribes, such as a retired Judge or a person with stated experience.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-fill the qualifications required in the facts of the main petition.
2. Option for the user to edit the petition to insert the particulars
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: VW: Note to Tech-Same as above-in the context of this defect.
defects.notes_2: Note from tech - We can do this it is possible but will need to specify to  the Agent to read the petition, so basically create a workflow for it
defects.ai_note:
Required qualifications usually sit in the arbitration clause, in words such as "shall be a retired", "qualification", "shall be a person" or "having experience in". Where the arbitration agreement is not clearly titled, use the agreement between the sides that contains an arbitration clause. Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition and the agreement by their own headings and the cause title.
Compliance needs, where the agreement requires any qualification of the arbitrators, (a) the qualification as prescribed in the agreement and (b) a statement of that qualification with the petition.
Do not treat the qualifications of an arbitrator already appointed, or a qualification proposed by one side in correspondence, as the qualification the agreement requires.
Return not_applicable when the shown arbitration clause positively shows that it prescribes no qualification for the arbitrators. Return defect_found only when the shown clause prescribes a qualification and the shown petition paragraph describing the clause omits it; quote the clause. Return compliant when the shown petition states each qualification the clause prescribes. Return needs_review when the clause or the petition's description of it is not in the excerpts, is illegible, or only part of it is shown.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 does not briefly state the general nature of the dispute and the points at issue
defects.requirement: A Petition under Section 11 must contain a brief synopsis describing the general nature of the dispute and the points at issue.
defects.trigger_words: disputes have arisen; nature of the dispute; points at issue; QUESTIONS OF LAW; BRIEF FACTS; differences arose
where_to_look: Main Petition: general nature of the dispute and the points at issue
The facts paragraphs, or a passage headed "SYNOPSIS" or "BRIEF FACTS", that summarise how the dispute arose.
A valid statement says briefly what the dispute is about and states the points at issue between the sides.
The summary in this Section 11 petition under its own Supreme Court cause title, not the grounds or the prayer.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for the user to edit the petition in Jubeex with Jubeex giving suggestions for autofilling details from available annexures such as arbitration agreement details
2. Option for the user to Re-upload petition
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.ai_note:
The summary usually sits in the facts paragraphs or in a short "SYNOPSIS", with lines such as "disputes have arisen" or "differences arose", followed by the points on which the sides disagree. Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a brief description of the general nature of the dispute and (b) a statement of the points at issue.
Do not treat the grounds for appointing an arbitrator, the prayer, or a bare statement that disputes exist as a description of the nature of the dispute and the points at issue.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when the shown facts paragraphs or synopsis deal with the dispute yet give no description of its nature or no points at issue; quote the passage. Return compliant when the shown excerpts describe the nature of the dispute and state the points at issue. Return needs_review when the facts or synopsis are not in the excerpts, are illegible, or only part of them is shown.

defects.defect: The Petition under Section 11 does not state the relief or remedy sought
defects.requirement: A Petition under Section 11 must state the relief or remedy sought.
defects.trigger_words: PRAYER; MAIN PRAYER; most respectfully prayed; appoint an arbitrator; pass such other order
where_to_look: Main Petition: relief or remedy sought
The paragraph headed "PRAYER" or "MAIN PRAYER", usually opening "It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed".
A valid prayer states in operative words the relief sought, such as the appointment of an arbitrator.
The prayer of this Section 11 petition under its own Supreme Court cause title, not the claims to be raised in the arbitration itself.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for the user to edit the petition to insert the particulars
(Jubeex should be able to suggest based on the cause-title of the petition)

Sub-section (4) or Sub-
section (5) or Sub-section (6) of Section 11
defects.location_source: Page 62 of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Section 11. Appointment of arbitrators.

Section 11 (4) If the appointment procedure in sub-section (3) applies and—
(a) a party fails to appoint an arbitrator within thirty days from the receipt of a request to do so from the other party; or (b) the two appointed arbitrators fail to agree on the third arbitrator within thirty days from the date of their appointment, the appointment shall be made, upon request of a party, by [the Supreme Court or, as the case may be,the High Court or any person or institution designated by such Court];

Section 11 (5) Failing any agreement referred to in sub-section (2), in an arbitration with a sole arbitrator, if the parties fail to agree on the arbitrator within thirty days from receipt of a request by one party from the other party to so agree the appointment shall be made, upon request of a party, by [the Supreme Court or, as the case may be, the High Court or any person or institution designated by such Court].
Section 11 (6) Where, under an appointment procedure agreed upon by the parties -

(a) a party fails to act as required under that procedure; or
(b) the parties, or the two appointed arbitrators, fail to reach an agreement expected of them under that procedure; or
(c) a person, including an institution, fails to perform any function entrusted to him or it under that procedure,
a party may request [the Supreme Court or, as the case may be, the High Court or any person or institution designated by such Court] to take the necessary measure, unless the agreement on the appointment procedure provides other means for securing the appointment.
defects.ai_note:
The averment usually sits in the sworn paragraphs above the "VERIFICATION", stating that the Section 11(4), 11(5) or 11(6) condition is met: a failure to appoint or agree on an arbitrator within thirty days of a request, or a failure to act under the agreed procedure. It cites a supporting document by nature and date. Labels may be wrong; identify the Affidavit by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) an Affidavit filed with the Section 11 petition, (b) an averment in it that the condition under sub-section (4), (5) or (6) of Section 11, as the case may be, was satisfied before the petition was made and (c) the relevant document supporting that averment.
Do not accept an affidavit that only verifies the petition as true, or an Annexure whose nature or date differs from the document the averment cites.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when the shown Affidavit, from heading to VERIFICATION, makes no averment that the condition was satisfied, or the Annexure cited as support is shown to be a different document; quote the relevant line. Return compliant when the shown excerpts establish the averment and the matching supporting document. Return needs_review when either is not in the excerpts, is illegible, or only part of the Affidavit is shown.

defects.location_source: Page 64 of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Order XIX Rule 6 applies to specified categories of certificate appeals and contempt appeals which, upon registration, are placed before the Supreme Court for ex parte preliminary hearing. At this stage, the Court may summarily dismiss the appeal, direct issuance of notice to the necessary parties, or pass such other orders as it deems fit. The categories of appeals covered are:

(i) Appeals against a judgment, decree or final order of a High Court summarily dismissing an appeal or other proceeding.

(ii) Certificate appeals where the High Court has granted a certificate under Article 134A of the Constitution, of the nature referred to in Article 132(1) (appeals involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution) or Article 133(1) (civil appeals involving a substantial question of law of general importance requiring decision by the Supreme Court), or under any other provision of law, without recording reasons or grounds for granting the certificate.

(iii) Appeals under Section 19(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, i.e., appeals to the Supreme Court as of right from an order or decision of a Bench of a High Court in the exercise of its contempt jurisdiction.

defects.trigger_words: INTERIM RELIEF; PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF; ex parte ad interim; pending the hearing; stay the operation; APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF; I.A. No
where_to_look: Main Petition: prayer for interim relief, if any
The "PRAYER" and any "PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF" in the Main Petition, such as a stay pending the hearing of the appeal.
An application seeking interim relief, such as one headed "APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF", filed with the Criminal Appeal.
The Main Petition bearing this Criminal Appeal's Supreme Court cause title, its prayers compared with the applications filed with it.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-draft the separate Interim Relief Application
2. Option for the User to add and edit the Interim Relief Application with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: Page 76-77 of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: VW Note to Tech: It will be applicable only in those cases where Interim Relief is Prayed for.
defects.ai_note:
Interim relief in a Criminal Appeal is usually sought in a paragraph headed "PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF" or in the prayer as "ex parte ad interim" relief or a stay pending the appeal. The separate application is usually headed "APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF" or "I.A. No. … of …" seeking stay or other interim relief. Labels may be wrong; identify the Criminal Appeal by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) whether interim relief is prayed for in the Criminal Appeal and (b) where it is, a separate application seeking that interim relief.
Do not treat the final prayer to set aside the order under appeal as a prayer for interim relief, or an application for another purpose, such as exemption, as one for interim relief.
not_applicable applies when the shown prayers of the Criminal Appeal seek no interim relief. Return defect_found only when the excerpts show a prayer for interim relief and the appeal itself states which applications accompany it with none seeking interim relief; quote the interim prayer. Return compliant when the excerpts show the interim prayer and a separate application seeking it; quote the application's heading. Return needs_review when the prayers are not in the excerpts, or interim relief is prayed for but no application is shown either way.

defects.defect: Separate application for interim relief has not been filed and/or the prayer for interim relief has been incorporated in the main appeal petition
defects.requirement: The main appeal petition must not incorporate a prayer for interim relief; where interim relief is sought in a Civil Appeal, a separate application for interim relief must be filed.
defects.trigger_words: PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF; ad interim; pending the hearing of this appeal; stay the operation; APPLICATION FOR STAY; APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF; I.A. No
where_to_look: Main Petition: any prayer for interim relief in the appeal
The "PRAYER" paragraph of the Civil Appeal and any paragraph headed "PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF" or seeking ad interim relief.
The interlocutory applications filed with the Civil Appeal, for one headed "APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF" or seeking stay.
A valid filing keeps the main prayer to final relief and asks for interim relief only by a separate application.
The Civil Appeal bearing this matter's Supreme Court cause title, not a stay order of a court below.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-draft the application.
2. Option for user to upload the application.
defects.location_source: Official source not recorded
defects.notes: VW Note to Tech: It will be applicable only in those cases where Interim Relief is Prayed for.
defects.ai_note:
Legal status: Needs legal verification. This status does not prevent a compliant finding when complete, legible filing evidence affirmatively satisfies every stated element. Return compliant according to the compliance instruction below. Until a current authoritative rule, form, circular, practice direction, statute, or binding judgment confirms the obligation and its applicability, convert any otherwise defect_found outcome to needs_review. Also return needs_review when any prerequisite evidence is unavailable.
In a Civil Appeal the reliefs appear under "PRAYER"; an interim prayer reads "pending the hearing of this appeal", "ad interim" or "stay the operation". A separate request is an interlocutory application headed "APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF", "APPLICATION FOR STAY" or "I.A. No. … of …". Labels may be wrong; identify the Civil Appeal by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the main appeal petition not incorporating a prayer for interim relief and (b) any interim relief sought being sought by a separate application.
Do not treat the final prayers, such as setting aside the decision under appeal, or the general prayer to pass such other order, as interim relief. A prayer for interim relief inside an interlocutory application is the correct form, not a defect.
not_applicable applies when the shown main prayer of the Civil Appeal seeks no interim relief and no shown application seeks it. Return defect_found when the shown prayer of the main Civil Appeal includes interim relief, whether or not a separate application is also filed; quote that prayer. Return compliant when the main prayer seeks only final relief and interim relief is sought in a separate application; quote the application's heading. Return needs_review when the prayer of the Civil Appeal is not in the excerpts or is illegible.

defects.defect: Separate application for interim relief has not been filed and/or the prayer for interim relief has been incorporated in the main appeal petition
defects.requirement: Where interim relief is sought in a Criminal Appeal, a separate application for interim relief must be filed, and the prayer for interim relief should not be incorporated in the main appeal petition.
defects.trigger_words: PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF; interim relief; ex parte ad interim; suspension of sentence; pending the disposal; APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF; I.A. No
where_to_look: Main Petition: prayer clause, for any interim relief sought
The prayer below the grounds of the Criminal Appeal, including any "PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF" such as suspension of sentence or stay.
Interlocutory applications filed with the Criminal Appeal, for a separate application seeking interim relief.
A compliant appeal seeks only final relief in its own prayer, with interim relief sought in its own application.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-draft the application.
2. Option for user to upload the application.
defects.location_source: Page 76-77, of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: VW Note to Tech: It will be applicable only in those cases where Interim Relief is Prayed for.
defects.ai_note:
In a Criminal Appeal, interim relief such as suspension of sentence, bail or stay is often sought in a paragraph headed "PRAYER FOR INTERIM RELIEF" or in the prayer as "ex parte ad interim" relief. A separate application is headed "APPLICATION FOR INTERIM RELIEF", "APPLICATION FOR SUSPENSION OF SENTENCE" or "I.A. No. … of …". Labels may be wrong; identify the Criminal Appeal by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a separate application where interim relief is sought and (b) no prayer for interim relief within the main appeal petition.
Do not treat the final prayer to set aside the conviction or the order under appeal as interim relief. Do not treat an exemption application as one for interim relief, and do not treat a mention of interim relief in the facts as a prayer.
not_applicable applies when the shown prayers and applications seek no interim relief. Return defect_found when the shown prayer of the main Criminal Appeal includes interim relief; quote that prayer. Return compliant when the main prayer shows only final relief and a separate application for interim relief is shown; quote both. Return needs_review when the prayer of the Criminal Appeal is not in the excerpts or is illegible.
Return defect_found only when the complete, correctly identified filing part provides positive evidence of every element of this defect. Return needs_review when evidence is absent, partial, illegible, contradictory, or depends on unavailable Registry-only metadata.

defects.defect: The Criminal Appeal does not contain the provisions of law under which the conviction has been recorded and the details of the sentence imposed, including fine, if any
defects.requirement: The Criminal Appeal must contain the provisions of law under which the conviction has been recorded and the details of the sentence imposed, including fine, if any.
defects.trigger_words: convicted under Section; sentenced to undergo; rigorous imprisonment; simple imprisonment; fine of Rs; in default of payment; punishable under Section
where_to_look: Main Petition: provisions of conviction and the sentence, with any fine
Annexures: Trial Court judgment recording conviction, sentence and fine
Impugned Order: operative paragraph confirming or altering the conviction and sentence.

The facts paragraphs of the Main Petition, such as "convicted under Section … and sentenced to undergo …"; compare each section, sentence and fine with the Trial Court judgment and the Impugned Order.
The Main Petition bearing this Criminal Appeal's Supreme Court cause title, not a sentence recited only in an order of a court below.
how_to_cure: 1. Prompt the User to enter the provision(s) of law under which the conviction has been recorded and the details of the sentence imposed, including the fine, if any, in the Criminal Appeal Petition.
2. Provide the User with an option to add and edit the provision(s) of law and sentence details entered in the Petition with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: Page 76-77 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes: Note to tech:- Better Approach is to Flag it but not get into what will be added or removed
defects.ai_note:
The Criminal Appeal usually states the conviction and sentence in its facts paragraphs, such as "convicted under Section … and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for … years with a fine of Rs. …". The Trial Court judgment in the Annexures and the Impugned Order record them in their operative paragraph. Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the provisions of law under which the conviction has been recorded, (b) the details of the sentence imposed and (c) the fine, if any, all stated in the Criminal Appeal.
Do not treat the sections in the FIR or the charge as the provisions of conviction, and do not take the details only from the Impugned Order or the Annexures; they must be stated in the Criminal Appeal.
not_applicable applies when the excerpts show the appeal is not against a conviction, such as an appeal against acquittal. Return defect_found when the shown Criminal Appeal states the conviction without its provisions or sentence, omits a fine the shown judgment imposed, or differs from the Impugned Order or Trial Court judgment; quote both lines. Return compliant when it states the provisions, the sentence and any fine; quote that line. Return needs_review when its statement of conviction is not in the excerpts or is illegible.
Return defect_found only when the complete, correctly identified filing part provides positive evidence of every element of this defect. Return needs_review when evidence is absent, partial, illegible, contradictory, or depends on unavailable Registry-only metadata.

defects.special_category: Criminal Appeal with High Court Certificate
defects.defect: The petition of appeal not accompanied by a certified copy of the judgment or order appealed from
defects.requirement: The petition of appeal must be accompanied by a certified copy of the judgment or order appealed from, as required by Order XX, Rule 2(2).
defects.trigger_words: CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY; Certified Copy; Copying Section; Date of application for copy; Date of delivery; Copyist; Examined by
where_to_look: Impugned Order: certification marks of a certified copy
The stamp "CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY" with the seal and signature of the court officer, and the copying endorsement giving the dates the copy was requested, made ready and delivered.
A valid copy is the full judgment or order appealed from, bearing the issuing court's certification; a typed, downloaded or plain copy is not a certified copy.
The Impugned Order bearing the cause title and date of the judgment under appeal in this Criminal Appeal, not an earlier order of a lower court.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to upload the certified copy of the judgment or order appealed from.
defects.location_source: Page 76-77 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.ai_note:
A certified copy carries the issuing court's endorsement, usually a stamp reading "CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY" or "Certified Copy", the court's seal, the copying officer's signature and a copying endorsement with the dates the copy was requested, made ready and delivered. Stamps, seals and signatures are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections. Labels may be wrong; identify the judgment by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a copy of the judgment or order appealed from and (b) that copy being certified by the court that issued it.
Do not treat a copy marked only "TRUE COPY" by counsel, a website download or a typed copy as certified, nor the certification of an earlier order of a lower court as certification of the judgment appealed from.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when the shown pages of the judgment appealed from positively show it is not a certified copy, such as a website download note or only a counsel's "TRUE COPY" mark, and no certification appears in the text or the visual detections; quote that line. Return compliant when the certification of that judgment is shown; quote it. Return needs_review when the judgment, or the pages that would bear the certification, are not in the excerpts or are illegible.

defects.special_category: Criminal Appeal with High Court Certificate
defects.defect: In the case of an appeal on a certificate, Criminal Appeal is not accompanied by the certificate granted by the High Court
defects.requirement: In an appeal on a certificate, the Criminal Appeal must be accompanied by the High Court's certificate granted in respect of the impugned judgment or order.
defects.trigger_words: fit case for appeal; fit one for appeal; certificate of fitness; certify that; certificate is granted; appeal to the Supreme Court
where_to_look: Impugned Order: certificate granted by the High Court for the appeal
Annexures: certificate of the High Court, if filed as an Annexure
A heading or passage in which the High Court certifies that the case is a fit one for appeal to the Supreme Court, with its date and the Bench that granted it.
The certificate bearing the same High Court case number as the Impugned Order, not a certificate issued in another case.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to upload the Certificate granted by HC with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: Page 77 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.ai_note:
Legal status: Needs legal verification. This status does not prevent a compliant finding when complete, legible filing evidence affirmatively satisfies every stated element. Return compliant according to the compliance instruction below. Until a current authoritative rule, form, circular, practice direction, statute, or binding judgment confirms the obligation and its applicability, convert any otherwise defect_found outcome to needs_review. Also return needs_review when any prerequisite evidence is unavailable.
The High Court's certificate may be a separate document headed "CERTIFICATE" or a passage stating that the case is a fit one for appeal to the Supreme Court; it bears the High Court's cause title, case number, date and signatures, which are often missing from OCR, so check the visual detections. Labels may be wrong; identify the certificate by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a certificate granted by the High Court for an appeal to the Supreme Court and (b) that certificate relating to the impugned judgment or order in this Criminal Appeal.
Do not treat a mere statement in the Criminal Appeal that a certificate was granted, or a certificate bearing a different High Court case number, as the certificate for this judgment.
not_applicable applies when the shown Criminal Appeal states that it is not an appeal on a certificate, for example an appeal by special leave. After legal verification is completed, return defect_found only when the excerpts state that the appeal is on a certificate and the pages filed as the certificate show something else, such as a refusal; quote that line. Return compliant when the High Court's certificate for this judgment is shown; quote its operative line. Return needs_review when the certificate is not in the excerpts, is illegible, or cannot be tied to this judgment.

defects.special_category: Criminal Appeal with High Court Certificate
defects.defect: In the case of an appeal on a certificate, Criminal Appeal is not accompanied by the order granting the said certificate.
defects.requirement: Where a Criminal Appeal is brought on a certificate, it must be accompanied by the order granting that certificate, passed in respect of the impugned judgment or order.
defects.trigger_words: certificate is granted; certificate prayed for; fit case for appeal; CORAM; ORAL ORDER; leave to appeal
where_to_look: Impugned Order: order of the High Court granting the certificate

An order with the High Court's cause title, "CORAM" and date whose operative line grants the certificate, such as "certificate is granted", or a closing paragraph of the impugned judgment granting it.
A valid order is signed and dated by the Bench and grants the certificate, rather than merely recording that one was asked for.
The order bearing the same High Court case number as the impugned judgment in this Criminal Appeal, not an order in another case or an order refusing the certificate.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to upload the order granting the certificate with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: Page 77 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.ai_note:
The order granting the certificate is usually a short High Court order with its cause title, "CORAM", date and an operative line such as "certificate is granted" or "this is a fit case for appeal"; sometimes the grant is made in the closing paragraph of the impugned judgment itself. Signatures and seals are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections. Labels may be wrong; identify the order by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) an order of the High Court granting the certificate and (b) that order relating to the impugned judgment or order in this Criminal Appeal.
Do not treat a statement in the Criminal Appeal that a certificate was granted, an order merely noting that a certificate was prayed for, or an order refusing the certificate as the order granting it. Do not use an order passed in another case.
not_applicable applies when the shown Criminal Appeal states that it is not an appeal on a certificate. Return defect_found only when the shown High Court order on the certificate refuses or does not grant it, or relates to another case; quote that line. Return compliant when an order granting the certificate for this judgment is shown; quote its operative line. Return needs_review when no such order is in the excerpts, or it is illegible.

defects.special_category: Criminal Appeal with High Court Certificate
defects.defect: The appeal is not accompanied by a certified copy (or an uncertified copy affirmed by affidavit as a true copy) of the judgment or order of the court immediately below.
defects.requirement: Where an appeal falls under Order XX Rule 5(1) of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, it must be accompanied by a certified copy of the judgment or order of the court immediately below, or an uncertified copy affirmed by affidavit as a true copy. Order XX Rule 5(1) covers (i) appeals against a judgment, final order or sentence of a High Court summarily dismissing a criminal appeal or other criminal proceeding; (ii) certificate appeals where the High Court has granted a certificate under Article 134A in respect of an appeal under Article 132(1) or Article 134(1)(c), or under any other provision of law, without recording reasons or grounds for granting the certificate; and (iii) appeals under Section 19(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, against an order or decision of a Bench of a High Court in the exercise of its contempt jurisdiction.
defects.trigger_words: certified to be true copy; Copying Section; Date of application for copy; summarily dismissed; dismissed in limine; Article 134A; Contempt of Courts Act; solemnly affirm
where_to_look: Annexures: judgment or order of the court immediately below
Impugned Order: whether it summarily dismissed or granted a bare certificate
On the copy of the lower court's judgment, the stamp "CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY" and the copying endorsement, or, for an uncertified copy, an affidavit stating that it is a true copy.
The judgment of the court from which the High Court's decision arose, such as the Trial Court or Sessions Court, not the High Court's impugned judgment itself.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for the User to upload the certified copy of the of the judgment or order of the court.
2.1. Option for  the User to upload the uncertified copies of the documents.

2.2. Option for Jubeex to draft an affidavit affirming that the copies are true copies of the documents forming part of the record of the Court sought to be appealed from, and prompt the User to have it duly sworn and upload the duly sworn affidavit with Jubeex.
2.3.  Option for the User to upload the affidavit with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: Page 76-77 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Order XX Rule 5(1) applies to specified categories of criminal certificate appeals and contempt appeals which, upon registration, are placed before the Supreme Court for ex parte preliminary hearing.The categories of appeals covered are:

(i) Appeals against a judgment, final order or sentence of a High Court summarily dismissing a criminal appeal or other criminal proceeding.

(ii) Certificate appeals where the High Court has granted a certificate under Article 134A of the Constitution, of the nature referred to in Article 132(1) (appeals involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution) or Article 134(1)(c) (criminal appeals certified by the High Court as fit for appeal to the Supreme Court), or under any other provision of law, without recording reasons or grounds for granting the certificate.

(iii) Appeals under Section 19(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, i.e., appeals to the Supreme Court as of right from an order or decision of a Bench of a High Court in the exercise of its contempt jurisdiction.
defects.ivan_comment: Ivan's comment:- They are talking about the order of the court below the High court, you have to anyway annex the judgement because it is important to explain the history of the case, it need not be certified
defects.ai_note:
The judgment of the court immediately below is usually an Annexure headed with that court's name, case number and "JUDGMENT". A certified copy bears a stamp such as "CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY", a seal and a copying endorsement, often missing from OCR, so check the visual detections; an uncertified copy needs an affidavit affirming it as a true copy. Labels may be wrong; identify the lower court's judgment by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the appeal falling within Order XX Rule 5(1), (b) a copy of the judgment or order of the court immediately below and (c) that copy being certified, or uncertified but affirmed by affidavit as a true copy.
Do not treat the High Court's impugned judgment as the judgment of the court immediately below, or a counsel's "TRUE COPY" mark as certification.
not_applicable applies when the excerpts show the appeal is none of the three kinds in Order XX Rule 5(1). Return defect_found only when the lower court's judgment is shown uncertified and the shown affidavit does not affirm it as a true copy; quote the line. Return compliant when the copy is shown certified or affirmed by affidavit; quote the mark or averment. Return needs_review when the judgment, its certification or the affidavit is not shown or is illegible.

defects.defect: The appeal does not state whether the appellant has surrendered. If he has surrendered, the petition is not accompanied by a certified copy of the order of the Court in which he has surrendered or a certificate of the competent officer of the Jail in which he is undergoing the sentence.
defects.requirement: The petition of appeal must state whether the person convicted has surrendered; if he has, it must be filed with a certified copy of the order of the Court in which he surrendered or a certificate of the competent officer of the Jail in which he is undergoing the sentence (Order XX, Rule 3).
defects.trigger_words: Whether accused/convict has surrendered; has surrendered; surrendered before; Superintendent of Jail; Jail Superintendent; undergoing sentence; Period of sentence undergone
where_to_look: Main Petition: statement whether the person convicted has surrendered
Annexures: surrender order or certificate of the Jail officer
Listing Proforma: field "Whether accused/convict has surrendered", read with the facts paragraph of the Main Petition on surrender.
A valid statement says plainly that he has or has not surrendered; where he has, the certified order or the Jail certificate must be of the Court or Jail named in that statement.
The Main Petition bearing this Criminal Appeal's Supreme Court cause title, not a bail order of a court below.
how_to_cure: 1. Surrender Status of the Appellant
1.1 Prompt the User to specify whether the appellant has surrendered and auto-fill the same in the Criminal Appeal Petition.
1.2 Option for the User to edit the surrender status in the Criminal Appeal Petition with Jubeex.
2. If he has surrendered, Option for the User to upload the certified copy of the surrender order or the certificate of the competent Jail Officer.
defects.location_source: SCR, 2013, Page 27 of the PDF 2024011691-1.pdf
defects.notes: Note to Tech:- If Appellant has not surrendered, allow him to draft application seeking exemption from surrendering with Jubeex
defects.ivan_comment: Ivan’s Comment: If the appellant has not surrendered, an application seeking exemption from surrendering is mandatory and cannot be ignored. If the appellant has surrendered, a custody certificate/order is required.
defects.ai_note:
Surrender is stated in a facts paragraph of the Criminal Appeal and the Listing Proforma row "Whether accused/convict has surrendered: Yes/No"; a blank cell is not printed, so a row showing other fields without it was left blank. A Jail certificate is often headed "CUSTODY CERTIFICATE"; its seal and signature may be missing from OCR, so check visual detections. Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a statement in the Criminal Appeal whether the person convicted has surrendered and (b) if he has, a certified copy of the surrender order of that Court or a certificate of the competent officer of the Jail where he is serving the sentence.
A bail order or an order suspending sentence is not a surrender order. The Listing Proforma entry supports, but does not replace, the appeal's statement.
not_applicable applies when the appeal is shown not to be by a convicted person. Return defect_found only when the appeal leaves the surrender status blank or unclear, or the document shown for a surrender is neither such an order nor such a certificate; quote the line. Return compliant when the status and any required order or certificate are shown; quote both. Return needs_review when the status or supporting document is not shown or is illegible.

defects.defect: The appellant has not surrendered and petition is not accompanied by an application seeking exemption from surrendering
defects.requirement: In a Criminal Appeal, where the person convicted has not surrendered, the petition must be accompanied by an application seeking exemption from surrendering (Order XX, Rule 3).
defects.trigger_words: EXEMPTION FROM SURRENDERING; exemption from surrender; Whether accused/convict has surrendered; yet to surrender; Surrender status; I.A. No
where_to_look: Listing Proforma: field "Whether accused/convict has surrendered"
Main Petition: statement whether the person convicted has surrendered
An application headed "APPLICATION FOR EXEMPTION FROM SURRENDERING" filed with the Criminal Appeal, where he has not surrendered.
A valid filing that records no surrender carries an application seeking exemption from surrendering for the person convicted in this appeal.
The application bearing this Criminal Appeal's Supreme Court cause title, not one seeking exemption from filing certified copies or other documents.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-generate the application seeking exemption from surrendering.
2. Option for the User to upload the application with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: SCR, 2013, Page 27 of the PDF 2024011691-1.pdf
defects.ai_note:
The surrender status appears in a facts paragraph of the Criminal Appeal and in the Listing Proforma row "Whether accused/convict has surrendered: Yes/No"; a blank cell is not printed, so a row listing other fields without this one was left blank. The application is usually headed "APPLICATION FOR EXEMPTION FROM SURRENDERING" or "I.A. No. … seeking exemption from surrender". Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the surrender status of the person convicted and (b) where he has not surrendered, an application seeking exemption from surrendering filed with the Criminal Appeal.
Do not treat an application for exemption from filing a certified copy, a translation or other documents, or a bail application made in a court below, as one for exemption from surrendering.
not_applicable applies when the excerpts show the person convicted has surrendered, or the appeal is not brought by a convicted person. Return defect_found only when the excerpts show he has not surrendered and the appeal states which applications accompany it, none seeking this exemption; quote the surrender line. Return compliant when non-surrender and the exemption application are both shown; quote its heading. Return needs_review when the surrender status is not shown or is illegible, or no application is shown either way.

defects.defect: The appellant is presenting the petition, praying for the restoration of the appeal, after the prescribed period of thirty days from the date of the dismissal order.
defects.requirement: Under Order XX Rule 11 of the Rules, where an appeal has been dismissed for non-prosecution in terms of Rule 10 thereof, the petition praying that the appeal may be restored must be presented within thirty days of the order of dismissal.
defects.trigger_words: dismissed for non-prosecution; non-prosecution; appeal may be restored; RESTORATION OF; for want of prosecution; CONDONATION OF DELAY
where_to_look: Main Petition: date of the order dismissing the appeal for non-prosecution

The paragraph of the restoration petition reciting the dismissal order and its date, the dismissal order in the Record of Proceedings or the Annexures, and the date of filing at the foot of the petition.
The Office Report on Limitation, which states the period from the dismissal order, and any application for condonation of delay filed with the restoration petition.
A petition presented within thirty days of the dismissal order is in time; count the days from the date of the order to the date of filing.
The restoration petition bearing this Criminal Appeal's Supreme Court cause title, not a petition to restore another matter.
Supreme Court Registry filing/refiling history or the relevant Registry order: use authoritative presentation dates and any period actually allowed; do not use a drafting date as proof of filing.
Return needs_review when the governing period or an authoritative date required for the calculation is unavailable.
how_to_cure: 1. Option for Jubeex to auto-draft an application for condonation of delay.

2. Option for the User to upload the CoD application with Jubeex.                                                                                       3. Option for User to draft an application for condonation of delay with Jubeex
defects.location_source: Page 82 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Order XX (11) - Where an appeal has been dismissed for non-prosecution, the appellant may, within thirty days of the 
order present a petition praying that the appeal may be restored and the Court may, after giving notice of the 
application to the respondent, if he has entered appearance, restore the appeal if good and sufficient cause is shown.
defects.ivan_comment:
Ask Ivan, is Condonation of Delay permitted for Application of Restoration filed beyond 30 days?


Ivan's comment:- Yes we, can. It can be included in the prayer. Generally COD is filed along with the applciation for restoration.  THIS APPLICATION IS USUALLY FILED SEPARATELY ONCE MAIN PETITION IS DISMISSED IN DEFAULT IT WONT BE FOUND "AFTER THE ANNEXURES" ALONG WITH THE MAIN PETITION
defects.ai_note:
A restoration petition is usually headed "APPLICATION FOR RESTORATION" and recites that the appeal was "dismissed for non-prosecution" or "for want of prosecution" on a stated date; the dismissal order appears in the Record of Proceedings or as an Annexure. Labels may be wrong; identify the restoration petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the date of the order dismissing the appeal for non-prosecution under Rule 10, (b) the date on which the petition for restoration was presented and (c) the second falling within thirty days of the first, as Order XX Rule 11 requires.
Count from the date of the dismissal order, not from receipt of its copy or any later order, and do not treat a dismissal on merits as one for non-prosecution. Whether good and sufficient cause is shown is for the Court, not this check.
not_applicable applies when the filing is not a petition to restore an appeal dismissed for non-prosecution. Return defect_found when both dates are shown, more than thirty days apart, and no application for condonation of delay is shown; quote both dates. Return compliant when the petition is within thirty days, or is later and such an application is shown; quote the dates. Return needs_review when either date is not in the excerpts or is illegible.
Return defect_found only when the complete, correctly identified filing part provides positive evidence of every element of this defect. Return needs_review when evidence is absent, partial, illegible, contradictory, or depends on unavailable Registry-only metadata.

defects.defect: Curative petition is not accompanied by a certificate of the Senior Advocate stating that the petition meets the requirements delineated in the judgment in Rupa Ashok Hurrah v. Ashok Hurrah (2002 INSC 189)
defects.requirement: A curative petition must be accompanied by a certificate of a Senior Advocate stating that the petition meets the requirements delineated in the judgment in Rupa Ashok Hurrah v. Ashok Hurrah (2002 INSC 189).
defects.trigger_words: Rupa Ashok Hurra; Rupa Ashok Hurrah; Senior Advocate; certified that; 2002 INSC 189; natural justice; apprehension of bias
where_to_look: AOR's Certificate: certificate signed by a Senior Advocate
Main Petition: the certificate, if printed below the prayer
A certificate stating that the curative petition meets the requirements laid down in "Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra" (2002 INSC 189).
The name and the designation "Senior Advocate" beside the signature at its foot, showing it was given by a designated Senior Advocate and not by the Advocate-on-Record.
The certificate bearing this curative petition's Supreme Court cause title, not a certificate filed with the earlier review petition.
how_to_cure: Prompt the User to obtain and upload the certificate of the Senior Advocate certifying that the Curative Petition meets the requirements laid down in Rupa Ashok Hurrah v. Ashok Hurrah, and review the same with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: Page 74 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Requirements delineated in the judgment in Rupa Ashok Hurrah v. Ashok Hurrah (2002 INSC 189) : - 
(1) violation of principles of natural justice in that he was not a party to the lis but the judgement adversely affected his interests or, if he was a party to the lis, he was not served with notice of the proceedings and the matter proceeded as if he had notice and 
(2) where in the proceedings a learned Judge failed to disclose his connection with the subject-matter or the parties giving scope for an apprehension of bias and the judgment adversely affects the petitioner. The petitioner, in the curative petition, shall aver specifically that the grounds mentioned therein had been taken in the review petition and that it was dismissed by circulation.
defects.ai_note:
The certificate is usually headed "CERTIFICATE" and reads "Certified that the Curative Petition meets the requirements delineated in Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra" (also spelt "Hurrah"), followed by the name of the Senior Advocate and the words "Senior Advocate". It may be labelled as the AOR's Certificate or sit within the Main Petition; signatures are often missing from OCR, so check the visual detections. Labels may be wrong; identify the certificate by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a certificate given by a designated Senior Advocate and (b) a statement in it that the petition meets the requirements in Rupa Ashok Hurrah v. Ashok Hurrah (2002 INSC 189), namely violation of natural justice or a Judge's undisclosed connection giving an apprehension of bias.
Do not treat the Advocate-on-Record's certificate, one by an advocate not designated as Senior Advocate, or the petition's own averments as this certificate.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when the shown certificate is signed by someone other than a Senior Advocate or does not state that the petition meets those requirements; quote its operative line. Return compliant when a Senior Advocate's certificate with that statement is shown; quote it. Return needs_review when the certificate is not in the excerpts, its signatory is unclear, or it is illegible.

defects.trigger_words: first curative petition; no other curative petition; filed earlier; previously filed; DECLARATION; is the first
where_to_look: Main Petition: statement that this is the first curative petition
The opening paragraphs of the curative petition, or a paragraph headed "DECLARATION", such as "This is the first curative petition …".
A valid disclosure states both that this is the first curative petition and that no other curative petition has been filed against the same judgment.
The curative petition bearing this matter's Supreme Court cause title, not a statement in the earlier review petition about other reviews.
how_to_cure: 1. Prompt the User to auto-fix and add the specific averment with Jubeex

Your Review has to be dismissed in chamber without open court hearing for curative petition to be maintainable

The disclosure usually sits in the opening paragraphs of the curative petition or in a short declaration, worded as "This is the first curative petition" or "No other curative petition has been filed against the impugned judgment". Labels may be wrong; identify the curative petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a statement that this is the first curative petition in the impugned matter and (b) a statement that no other curative petition has been filed earlier.
Do not treat a statement that no other review petition was filed, or that no similar matter is pending, as this disclosure, and do not treat a statement made in the review petition as one made in this curative petition.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. defects.defect: Curative petition not accompanied by a certified or authenticated copy of the judgment or order challenged.
defects.requirement: A curative petition must be accompanied by a certified or authenticated copy of the judgment or order challenged.
defects.trigger_words: CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY; Certified Copy; authenticated copy; Branch Officer; Assistant Registrar; REPORTABLE
where_to_look: Impugned Order: certification or authentication of the copy filed
The endorsement "CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY" or an authentication mark, with the seal and signature of the issuing officer, on the judgment or order challenged.
A valid copy is the complete judgment or order complained of, certified or authenticated by the court that passed it; a plain photocopy or printout is not enough.
The judgment or order challenged by this curative petition, identified by its own cause title and date, not a judgment of a lower court quoted in it.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to upload the certified or authenticated copy of the judgment or order complained of with Jubeex.
defects.location_source: Page 74 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.ai_note:
A certified copy of the decision complained of carries "CERTIFIED TO BE TRUE COPY" with the seal and signature of the issuing officer; an authenticated copy carries a similar authentication mark. These marks are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections. Labels may be wrong; identify the judgment by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a copy of the judgment or order challenged and (b) that copy being certified or authenticated by the court that issued it.
Do not treat a printout from a law report or court website, a copy marked only "TRUE COPY" by counsel, or a certified copy of a different judgment, such as one of the High Court, as a certified or authenticated copy of the judgment challenged.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability.
