defects.ai_note:
The prayer shows the kind of bail: "anticipatory bail" means anticipatory bail, while "release on regular bail" or "in custody since" means the accused is in custody. A Custody Certificate is issued by the jail Superintendent, names the accused, the jail and the period in custody, and carries the jail seal. Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a finding that the bail matter is not one for anticipatory bail and, if so, (b) a Custody Certificate on the file and (c) that certificate relating to the accused in this bail matter.
An averment in the Main Petition or bail application that the accused is in custody is not a Custody Certificate. A certificate of a co-accused or for another case does not serve. Seals and signatures are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections for them.
Return not_applicable when the excerpts show the matter is for anticipatory bail. Return defect_found only when the matter is shown to be a non-anticipatory bail matter and the certificate shown names another person or case; quote its name line. Return compliant when a Custody Certificate for the accused is shown; quote it. Return needs_review when the kind of bail or the certificate cannot be read in the excerpts.

defects.defect: Clear and Legible copy of Synopsis and List of Dates/Events is not filed
defects.requirement: Clear and Legible copy of Synopsis and List of Dates/Events must be filed
defects.trigger_words: DATES; EVENTS; PARTICULARS; Hence the present; Hence this Special Leave Petition
where_to_look: Synopsis: legibility of the narrative text
List of Dates & Events: legibility of each date and event entry
The Synopsis narrative and the List of Dates table with its "DATES" and "EVENTS" or "PARTICULARS" columns, ending with "Hence the present" petition.
A legible copy reads as continuous text with dates and events that can be made out; garbled characters and blurred or cut-off lines show illegibility.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to re-upload a clear and legible copy of the Synopsis and List of Dates/Eventswith Jubeex.
defects.ai_note:
The Synopsis is a short narrative of the case; the List of Dates & Events is usually a table with "DATES" and "EVENTS" or "PARTICULARS" columns, and it often ends with "Hence the present Special Leave Petition". Illegibility shows as broken or garbled OCR text, or a visual note of a blurred, faded or cut-off page. Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a clear and legible Synopsis and (b) a clear and legible List of Dates & Events.
Do not treat a few OCR misreadings in otherwise readable text as illegibility, and do not judge either document by the legibility of the facts in the petition. Check the visual detections for blurred, faded or cut-off pages before relying on OCR quality.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when shown pages of either document are largely unreadable; quote the garbled text. Return compliant when the shown pages of both documents read clearly. Return needs_review when either document is not in the excerpts, or legibility cannot be judged from the text and the visual detections.

defects.defect: Clear and Legible copy of impugned judgement is not filed
defects.requirement: Clear and Legible copy of impugned judgement must be filed
defects.trigger_words: CORAM; JUDGMENT; Heard learned counsel; Pronounced on; Date of Decision
where_to_look: Impugned Order: legibility of the impugned judgment text
The cause title, "CORAM", the body of reasoning and the operative paragraph with the date and signature lines of the impugned judgment.
A legible copy reads as continuous sentences; garbled or missing characters across most lines, or a blurred, faded or cut-off page in the visual detections, show illegibility.
The impugned judgment named in paragraph 1 of the Main Petition, carrying the court, case number and date given there.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to re-upload a clear and legible copy of the Impugned Judgment with Jubeex.
defects.ai_note:
The impugned judgment opens with the court's name, the case number, "CORAM" and often "Date of Decision" or "Pronounced on", and closes with the operative order and the Judge's name. OCR of a poor copy shows strings of broken characters, run-together words or blank stretches. Labels may be wrong; identify the impugned judgment by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a copy of the impugned judgment on the file and (b) that copy being clear and legible throughout.
Isolated OCR misreadings in otherwise readable text are not illegibility. A legible copy of a lower court's order does not make an illegible impugned judgment legible. Check the visual detections for blurred, faded, skewed or cut-off pages.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when shown pages of the impugned judgment are largely unreadable in both the text and the visual detections; quote the garbled passage. Return compliant when the shown pages read clearly. Return needs_review when the impugned judgment is not in the excerpts or legibility cannot be judged.

defects.defect: Signed, Clear and Legible copy of SLP with Certificate & Affidavit is not filed
defects.requirement: The Main Petition (SLP), the AOR's Certificate and the Affidavit must each be filed as signed, clear and legible copies.
defects.trigger_words: Filed by; Drawn & Filed by; confined only to the pleadings; DEPONENT; VERIFICATION; SOLEMNLY AFFIRM
where_to_look: Main Petition: signature of the Advocate-on-Record and legibility
AOR's Certificate: signature and legibility of the certificate

The "Filed by" or "Drawn & Filed by" line below the prayer of the SLP, the signature below "confined only to the pleadings" in the Certificate, and the deponent's signature and attestation at the foot of the Affidavit.
Each of the three documents must read clearly; garbled text, cut-off lines or a blurred page in the visual detections show illegibility.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to re-upload signed, clear and legible copies of the  Certificate and Affidavit with Jubeex.
defects.ai_note:
The SLP ends with the prayer and a signature beside "Filed by" or "Drawn & Filed by". The AOR's Certificate begins "Certified that the Special Leave Petition is confined only to the pleadings" and is signed by the Advocate-on-Record. The Affidavit carries the deponent's signature below the "VERIFICATION" and the notary or oath commissioner's attestation. Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a signed, clear and legible SLP, (b) a signed, clear and legible AOR's Certificate and (c) a signed, clear and legible Affidavit.
A typed name without a signature is not a signature, and the signature on one document does not cover the others. A few OCR misreadings in readable text are not illegibility. Signatures, seals and stamps are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections for each signature.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when a shown signature block of any of the three is blank in both the text and the visual detections, or a shown page is largely unreadable; quote the signature line or the garbled text. Return compliant when the shown excerpts establish the signature and legibility of all three. Return needs_review when any of the three, or its signature block, is not in the excerpts or is illegible.

defects.defect: Clear and Legible copy of Annexures is not filed
defects.requirement: Each Annexure must be filed as a clear and legible copy.
defects.trigger_words: TRUE COPY; TRUE TYPED COPY; Annexure P-1; Annexure A-1; Annexure-P
where_to_look: Annexures: legibility of the text of each Annexure
The "ANNEXURE P-1" or "A-1" marking and the "TRUE COPY" line at the top of each Annexure, and the body text under it.
A legible Annexure reads as continuous text in which names, dates, figures and seals can be made out; blurred, faded, cut-off or garbled text marks an illegible copy.
Each Annexure identified by its own Annexure marking and this matter's Supreme Court cause title, as distinct from a passage of the same document quoted in the Main Petition.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to re-upload  clear and legible copies of the Annexures with Jubeex.
defects.ivan_comment: [ONLY LAST PAGE OF EACH ANNEXURE NEEDS TO BE SIGNED]
defects.ai_note:
Each Annexure usually opens with a marking such as "ANNEXURE P-1", "Annexure A-1" or "Annexure-P/2", often with a "TRUE COPY" or "TRUE TYPED COPY" line, followed by the copied document. A poor scan shows up as broken words, random characters, missing lines or very little text for a full page. Labels may be wrong; identify each Annexure by its own marking and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) every Annexure shown to be a clear copy and (b) its text to be legible enough to read names, dates and figures.
Do not treat a passage of the document quoted in the Main Petition or in an application as the Annexure itself. A clean typed copy of one Annexure does not cure an illegible scan of another. Seals, stamps and handwriting are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections before calling a page illegible.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found only when a shown Annexure is plainly unreadable in substantial part, with garbled, faded or cut-off text; name that Annexure and quote a garbled line. Return compliant when the Annexures shown read clearly and nothing suggests a poor copy. Return needs_review when no Annexure is in the excerpts, or when it is unclear whether poor text comes from the copy itself or from OCR.

defects.defect: Clear and Legible copy of necessary applications is not filed
defects.requirement: Every necessary application filed with the SLP must be a clear and legible copy.
defects.trigger_words: INTERLOCUTORY APPLICATION; I.A. No.; APPLICATION FOR; MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH; PRAYER; Application seeking
where_to_look: Application: legibility of each application filed with the SLP
The heading "INTERLOCUTORY APPLICATION", "I.A. No." or "APPLICATION FOR", the averments under "MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH" and the "PRAYER".
A legible application reads as continuous text whose heading, averments and prayer can be made out; blurred, faded, cut-off or garbled text marks an illegible copy.
Each application bearing this matter's Supreme Court cause title, as distinct from a bail application of the court below quoted in the Main Petition.

No." or "APPLICATION FOR EXEMPTION FROM", then "MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH", numbered averments and a "PRAYER". Do not count a bail application of the High Court or trial court that is merely quoted or described in the Main Petition as one of the applications filed here. Seals and handwriting are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections before treating a page as illegible.
not_applicable applies only when the excerpts make clear that no application is filed or needed in this matter. Return defect_found when a shown application is unreadable in substantial part; name it and quote a garbled line. Return compliant when every application shown reads clearly. Return needs_review when no application is in the excerpts, or when it is unclear whether poor text comes from the copy itself or from OCR.
Return defect_found only when the complete, correctly identified filing part provides positive evidence of every element of this defect. Return needs_review when evidence is absent, partial, illegible, contradictory, or depends on unavailable Registry-only metadata.

defects.defect: Clear and Legible copy of Memo of parties is not filed

where_to_look: Memo of Parties: legibility of each party's name and address
The entries under "IN THE MATTER OF" and "VERSUS", each "Petitioner No." and "Respondent No." with its S/o, R/o and address lines.
A legible Memo of Parties lets every name, description, status and address be read; blurred, faded, cut-off or garbled entries mark an illegible copy.
The Memo of Parties bearing this matter's Supreme Court cause title, as distinct from the parties named in the Impugned Order of the court below.

Compliance needs (a) the Memo of Parties to be a clear copy and (b) every party's name, description and address in it to be legible.
Do not judge legibility from the party names printed in the Impugned Order or in the cause title of an application; only the Memo of Parties counts. Handwriting and seals are often missing from OCR; check the visual detections before calling a page illegible.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return defect_found when a shown part of the Memo of Parties is unreadable, such as a garbled name or address; quote that entry. Return compliant when the shown Memo of Parties reads clearly for every party listed. Return needs_review when the Memo of Parties is not in the excerpts, only part of it was shown, or it is unclear whether poor text comes from the copy or from OCR.
Return defect_found only when the complete, correctly identified filing part provides positive evidence of every element of this defect. Return needs_review when evidence is absent, partial, illegible, contradictory, or depends on unavailable Registry-only metadata.

Compliance needs (a) the petition in writing, (b) the name of the High Court or Civil Court where the case is pending, (c) the grounds on which transfer is sought and (d) a supporting affidavit.
The court to which transfer is sought is not the court where the case is pending. An affidavit filed in the pending case itself, or an order of the court below, is not the supporting affidavit for this petition.

defects.notes:
Article 139A, Constitution of India:- 
(1) Where cases involving the same or
substantially the same questions of law are pending
before the Supreme Court and one or more High Courts
or before two or more High Courts and the Supreme
Court is satisfied on its own motion or on an application
made by the Attorney-General of India or by a party to
any such case that such questions are substantial
questions of general importance, the Supreme Court may
withdraw the case or cases pending before the High Court
or the High Courts and dispose of all the cases itself:
Provided that the Supreme Court may after
determining the said questions of law return any case so
withdrawn together with a copy of its judgment on such
questions to the High Court from which the case has
been withdrawn, and the High Court shall on receipt
thereof, proceed to dispose of the case in conformity
with such judgment.

It is located in AOR certificate after main petition - 

It's not the same certificate as goes along with SLP
defects.ai_note:
The certificate usually reads "Certified that the case involves substantial questions of general importance", refers to Article 139A(1) and is signed by the Advocate-on-Record. Article 139A(1) lets the Court withdraw cases involving the same or substantially the same questions of law pending before it and one or more High Courts, or before two or more High Courts, where those are substantial questions of general importance. Labels may be wrong; identify the certificate by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a certificate of the Advocate-on-Record accompanying the transfer application and (b) its certification that the case involves substantial questions of general importance.
A routine certificate that the petition has been drafted and is in order does not satisfy (b). A statement in the petition itself that the questions are important is not the Advocate-on-Record's certificate.

The heading of the writ petition, which often recites the Article invoked, paragraph 1 below "MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH", and the paragraphs under "GROUNDS".

defects.ai_note:

Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) identification of the fundamental right relied on, by its Article or by its content, and (b) a statement of the nature of its infringement.
A bare recital of Article 32 as the source of jurisdiction does not identify the right infringed. Statutory or ordinary legal rights pleaded in the grounds are not fundamental rights. Whether the claim succeeds on merits is not for this check.

defects.requirement: The Main Petition must state both the relief sought, in its prayer, and the grounds for that relief; Order XXXVIII, Rule 7 requires this of every petition under Article 32 for a direction, order or writ (mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo-warranto etc.).

where_to_look: Main Petition: relief sought in the prayer and the grounds
The paragraph headed "PRAYER", often opening "It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed", and the lettered or numbered paragraphs under "GROUNDS".
A valid prayer names the specific writ, direction or order sought; valid grounds are the reasons relied on in support of that relief.
The writ petition under Article 32 bearing this matter's Supreme Court cause title, its main prayer rather than a prayer for interim relief.

defects.ai_note:

The grounds appear under "GROUNDS", usually as lettered or numbered paragraphs. Labels may be wrong; identify the Main Petition by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a statement of the relief sought and (b) the grounds on which that relief is sought.
A prayer for interim relief alone is not the relief sought in the writ petition, and the residuary clause "pass such other order" alone does not state a relief. Narrated facts are not grounds unless they are put forward as reasons for the relief. The strength of the grounds is not for this check.

OCR may print "DEPONENT" as "DEPONANT". Labels may be wrong; identify the Affidavit by its own heading and cause title.

The disclosure usually sits in the opening or procedural-history paragraphs, or in a separate paragraph such as "The petitioner has not filed any other petition seeking similar relief before any High Court". defects.ai_note:
A habeas corpus petition names the person restrained, often the "detenu", and prays for a writ of "Habeas Corpus" (OCR: "Habeus Corpus"). The Synopsis, List of Dates and paragraph 1 of the petition state which judgment or order is challenged and its date. Labels may be wrong; identify the Impugned Order by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a copy of a judgment or order of the court below and (b) its court, case number and date matching the judgment or order challenged in this Special Leave Petition.
An order of a lower forum that the challenged judgment merely affirmed is not the impugned order unless the petition challenges it. A quotation of the impugned order inside the petition, or an interim order in the same case, is not a copy of it.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. After legal verification is completed, return defect_found only when the shown copy is legible and its court, case number or date differs from the judgment or order the petition says it challenges; quote both. Return compliant when a shown copy matches the challenged judgment or order; quote its heading and date. Return needs_review when the copy or the petition's description of the challenged order is not in the excerpts or is illegible.

The heading "FILING INDEX" or "MEMO OF FILING", its table with columns such as "Sl. No.", "Particulars of Documents" and "No. of Pages", and the "Filed by" line.
A valid Filing Memo is a memo or index of the papers being filed in this matter, distinct from the paper-book Index.

The Filing Memo usually carries a heading such as "FILING INDEX" or "MEMO OF FILING", a short table of the papers filed with columns such as "Sl. No.", "Particulars of Documents" and "No. of Pages", and a "Filed by" line; it often comes late in the file, so its pages may be labelled as an Appendix or Application. Labels may be wrong; identify the Filing Memo by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a Filing Memo or Filing Index (b) for this matter.
The main paper-book Index, which lists every document with page numbers, is not the Filing Memo unless it is headed as a filing index. A list of documents inside an Appendix or Application is not the Filing Memo.

The table or list under the "DATES" and "EVENTS" columns, usually closing with "Hence the present" petition.
A valid list runs from the earliest date to the latest, gives a material fact or event against each date and, wherever applicable, refers to the relevant Annexure against the matching date.
The list bearing this matter's Supreme Court cause title, not a chronology reproduced from the Impugned Order or the courts below.

The list is usually a two-column table headed "DATES" and "EVENTS", or a run of dated paragraphs, often printed with the Synopsis under "SYNOPSIS AND LIST OF DATES" and closing with "Hence the present" petition. Each table row arrives as "DATES: …" and "EVENTS: …"; a blank cell is not printed, so a row with a date but no event shows the event was left blank. Labels may be wrong; identify the List of Dates & Events by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the dates arranged in chronological order and (b) the relevant material facts or events set out against each date.
Do not treat the narrative Synopsis, a chronology quoted in the Impugned Order, or dates in the petition's facts as this list. Annexure references against dates are expected wherever applicable.
Return not_applicable when the filing type, document type, or procedural prerequisite for this check is not established; trigger words alone do not establish applicability. Return compliant when the shown entries run in date order with an event against each; quote the first and last dates shown. Return needs_review when the list is not in the excerpts, is illegible, or too little of it is shown to judge the order.

The executant's line in the Vakalatnama, such as "through its Director" or "Authorised Signatory", and in the resolution the clause beginning "RESOLVED THAT".
A valid authorisation is issued by the same company, society or body and names the person who executed the Vakalatnama, or that person's office, as authorised to appoint and engage the Advocate.

When a body executes the Vakalatnama (also "Vakalat Nama", "Vakalath"), the executant line usually reads "through its Director", "Secretary" or "Authorised Signatory". The authorising document is usually a Board Resolution extract opening "RESOLVED THAT", or a letter of authority or Power of Attorney. Labels may be wrong; identify the Vakalatnama by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) a Vakalatnama executed on behalf of a company, society or other body and (b) a Board Resolution or other document authorising the executant to appoint and engage the Advocate for that body.
The Advocate-on-Record's acceptance on the Vakalatnama is not the body's authorisation. A resolution authorising someone else, or issued by a different body, does not cover this executant. A Memo of Appearance names the advocate, not the body's authority.
Return not_applicable when the shown Vakalatnama is executed by individuals in their own right and not for a company, society or other body. After legal verification is completed, return defect_found only when the shown authorising document names a different person or confers no power to engage an Advocate; quote its operative line. Return compliant when a shown resolution or document authorises this executant; quote the "RESOLVED THAT" line or its equivalent. Return needs_review when the executant's capacity or the authorising document is not in the excerpts or is illegible.

defects.defect: The petition has not been filed within the prescribed period of limitation.
defects.requirement: The applicable limitation period must be determined from the governing statute or Supreme Court Rule for the identified proceeding. Compliance must be calculated using the legally relevant impugned-order date, certified-copy application and readiness dates where applicable, permitted exclusions, and authoritative Supreme Court Registry filing/refiling timestamps. Do not infer limitation from a generic period or from drafting dates in uploaded pleadings.
defects.trigger_words: Limitation; Delay; condonation of delay; Date of Impugned Order; within limitation; Date of Judgment
where_to_look: Main Petition, Cover Page, and Listing Proforma: identify the proceeding type, governing provision, impugned decision, and dates asserted by the filer.
Impugned Order: authoritative pronouncement or order date.
Certified-copy record where legally relevant: application date, ready date, delivery date, and any period claimed for exclusion.
Supreme Court Registry filing and refiling history: authoritative initial filing and subsequent refiling timestamps.
The governing limitation provision and any pleaded exclusion, extension, or condonation application.
Return needs_review if the applicable period or any legally necessary date is missing, disputed, or available only from a non-authoritative drafting date.
how_to_cure: File an Application for Condonation of Delay
defects.location_source: Page 105-108, Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.ai_note:
The impugned date appears on the Impugned Order itself, below the cause title on the Cover Page, in the Listing Proforma and in paragraph 1 of the Main Petition. A delay is usually admitted in an Application for "condonation of delay". Labels may be wrong; identify each document by its own heading and cause title.
Compliance needs (a) the date of the impugned judgment or order, (b) the date of filing and (c) filing within the prescribed period of limitation applicable to the case.
Do not use a lower forum's earlier order date or the hearing date as the impugned date. Do not invent a limitation period; apply only the period prescribed for this case type.
Return not_applicable when the shown text shows that no period of limitation applies to this case type, such as a writ petition under Article 32. Return defect_found only when both dates are legible, the period is clear, the filing is beyond it and the shown text gives no sign of an Application for condonation of delay; quote the date lines. Return compliant when the filing is within the period, or the delay is the subject of a shown Application for condonation of delay; quote the date lines. Return needs_review when either date or the applicable period cannot be established from the excerpts.
